answer: In an agent marketplace trading crystal and jade, each seller must lock a bond, and its maximum unsettled sales are capped by that bond. At each settlement pulse, escrow releases payment only after delivery is verified; proven nondelivery forfeits the bond. Splitting into a thousand identities creates no extra sales capacity without a thousand bonds. The attacker must tie up capital proportional to the exposure it creates and risks losing that capital on fraudulent trades.
